analysis: Cross-source read: the morning's axis is the AI-capex debate. On one side, Michael Burry's fresh accounting critique (MSFT's ~$300B uncommenced leases and 15-to-25-year life stretch, AMZN's commitments +81% to ~$267B with LT debt doubled to $128.9B, META's ~$700B off-balance-sheet, GOOGL's nearly $900B) argues for massive write-offs in two years. On the other side, Anthropic just committed a minimum $11.6B (up to ~$20B) to Akamai over seven years plus a 5% equity warrant, and chip stocks are +2% each in premarket — demand is being signed, not just spent. Futures are green because the AI bid is absorbing the yield shock, but the shock is real: the 10Y touched its highest since 2007 on Thursday and sits at ~5.18%, and October-hike odds jumped to 71% from ~50% early in the week. Thursday's session closed mixed (S&P ~flat, Nasdaq barely green, Dow down a third straight day) — resilience, not capitulation. What changed vs the 9 AM Thursday brief: Costco's Q4 landed (EPS beat on a $0.15 tariff-refund one-off, membership-fee growth slowed a third straight quarter, stock muted); the Tesla Semi event happened (customer deliveries starting, but no volume or pricing disclosed, feeding the sell-the-news setup); the Trump-Xi dinner happened (cordial, no breakthroughs, but Musk/Huang/Lisa Su/Cook seated at the leaders' table puts semis and AI at the center of any follow-up commentary); Williams' 'reasonable' hike remark is now joined by Paulson and Hammack, and FedWatch odds stepped up from 64% to 71%. Signal vs noise: futures levels, the 10Y print, FedWatch odds, Costco's reported numbers, Akamai's deal terms, the Tesla event facts, and the dinner guest list are confirmed across outlets; Burry's piece is a single-source relay of his own writing (treat as one investor's bear case, not reporting); WTI/Brent exact levels conflict across sources (direction — lower on Iran talks — is agreed); Costco's after-hours move is reported as flat to +0.2% across outlets. No qualifying HN/Reddit threads surfaced with verifiable URLs.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: Futures pointed higher early Friday: at 05:15 a.m. ET, Dow E-minis were up 162 points (+0.31%), S&P 500 E-minis up 23.75 (+0.31%), Nasdaq 100 E-minis up 188 (+0.61%), as AI enthusiasm offset worries over high oil prices and Treasury yields. The 10Y stood near 5.18%, down ~3 bps from Thursday's close but off overnight highs above 5.2%.
headlines.why_it_matters: The AI bid is absorbing the yield shock into the open — whether the bid holds once cash trading starts, with the 10Y still at two-decade highs, is the morning's tape question.

headlines.headline: Anthropic committed to pay Akamai at least $11.6 billion over seven years for cloud infrastructure and software (WSJ), with a potential $9 billion expansion to ~$20 billion total, plus a warrant for ~7.7 million shares (~5% at $111.33). Akamai shares surged 21-23% in premarket trading; the company adds ~$1.7B of capex this year with no 2026 revenue contribution from the deal.
headlines.why_it_matters: A signed demand-side datapoint for the AI-infrastructure trade — the counterweight to the AI-capex bear case; the capex-first, revenue-later structure is why the stock popped but guidance didn't move.

headlines.headline: Michael Burry sounded a fresh alarm on big-tech AI spending, warning of massive write-offs in two years: Microsoft nearly tripled uncommenced leases to over $300B while extending data-center useful lives from 15 to 25 years; Amazon's uncommitted leases/purchase commitments surged 81% to ~$267B while long-term debt doubled to $128.9B; Meta faces ~$700B in off-balance-sheet commitments; Alphabet nearly $900B.
headlines.why_it_matters: Single-source relay of one investor's accounting critique — treat as fragile as a tape catalyst, but it is the coherent bear case on the AI-capex complex, and it lands the same morning as the Anthropic-Akamai deal.

headlines.headline: Costco's fiscal Q4 beat on a one-off: EPS $6.75 vs ~$6.52-6.54 expected, including a $0.15/share non-recurring benefit from Trump tariff refunds; revenue $95.72B beat (~$94.89B est); comparable sales +9.4% (+6.7% ex gas/currency); membership-fee income grew 7.3%, its third straight quarter of slowing growth; e-commerce +19.5%. Shares were muted after hours (roughly flat to +0.2%).
headlines.why_it_matters: A quality-of-beat story — the EPS beat rested on a tariff-refund one-off, not accelerating core comps, which is why the stock didn't move at ~40x forward earnings.

headlines.headline: Tesla began customer deliveries of its Semi trucks this week from the new Sparks, Nevada plant, which is designed for 50,000 trucks a year (planned capacity, not current rate). The 325-mile Standard and 500-mile Long Range variants ride an 800-kW three-motor powertrain; Musk (pre-recorded video) teased self-driving 'in the very near future' and a 'pretty significant' waiting list. Tesla disclosed no production volume plans or pricing. TSLA edged higher early Friday.
headlines.why_it_matters: A real production milestone after nine years, but with no volume or pricing disclosed the 'sell the news' overhang stands — 8 of 10 prior Tesla events traded lower a week later.

headlines.headline: Meta is set for its fifth straight week of gains — its biggest five-week gain since late January 2023 — putting it less than 1% away from a $2 trillion market value, on traction for its Muse AI app among young consumers and the Charm AI device. META traded flat in premarket.
headlines.why_it_matters: The decoupling keeps widening — META led communication services' weekly gains even as yields climbed, because the market is pricing it as an AI-monetization story, not a rates victim.

headlines.headline: Chip stocks led the premarket bid: AMD, Marvell, Cerebras and Intel rose ~2% each, with NVDA and TSLA also marginally higher, as AI optimism offset rate and oil worries. Bernstein's Buy reaffirmation on NVDA from Thursday carried into the tape.
headlines.why_it_matters: Hardware is the tip of the AI-enthusiasm spear this morning — the Anthropic-Akamai deal and the premarket chip bid reinforce each other while rates pressure the rest of tech.

headlines.headline: Traders see a 71% chance the Fed hikes at least 25 bps in October, up from around 50% earlier this week (CME FedWatch via Reuters). Investopedia put the chance of at least one more hike at the year's final two meetings at 95%, after hawkish turns from Paulson, Hammack, and Williams within 24 hours.
headlines.why_it_matters: The repricing is deepening, not done — each leg up in hike odds re-taxes growth multiples, which is why futures strength this morning lives next to a 5.18% 10Y.

headlines.headline: Thursday evening's Trump-Xi state dinner was cordial — Trump said the US and China had 'never gotten along better,' Xi said talks 'added new substance' — with Musk, Huang, AMD's Lisa Su, and Cook seated at the leaders' table, plus Altman, Bezos, Zuckerberg, Nadella, and Pichai among 100+ guests; no Chinese corporate CEOs attended. The Busan trade-suspension extension to January 10 stands.
headlines.why_it_matters: Seating the chip and tech CEOs with the two leaders put semiconductors and AI at the summit's center — any follow-up comment on export controls, rare earths, or AI regulation is today's swing factor for NVDA, AMD, and China-exposed megacaps.

market_snapshot.breadth_notes: Prior regular session (Thu) close: S&P 500 ~flat (-0.02%), Nasdaq +0.01% to 26,939.37, Dow -0.31% (third straight down day), Russell 2000 -0.11% — a mixed close off morning lows, resilience rather than capitulation. Weekly entering Friday: Nasdaq +1.6%, S&P 500 +0.7%, Dow -0.6% (pace for fourth straight weekly loss); communication services and tech led weekly gains. S&P 500 and Nasdaq a little more than 1% from record highs. Advance/decline, volume vs 20-day average, and VIX not shown on sourced pages — unavailable. Premarket Fri ~05:15 ET: Dow +0.31%, S&P +0.31%, Nasdaq 100 +0.61% (Reuters).
market_snapshot.notes: 2.5h before the open Fri: futures green on the AI bid (AKAM +21-23% on the Anthropic deal, chips +2%) against a 5.18% 10Y and $100+ Brent. Overnight: Costco Q4 beat on a tariff-refund one-off (stock muted), Tesla Semi customer deliveries began (no volume/pricing), Trump-Xi dinner cordial with chip CEOs at the top table, and Burry's AI-capex write-off warning circulated. October-hike odds jumped to 71% (FedWatch).

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC news overnight — carried context stands: the Sept 9/10 $600M 6.75% senior notes pricing (due 2035, net ~$592M to repay credit borrowings) and the NYSE-to-TXSE listing transfer (NYSE trading ends Oct 2, TXSE begins Oct 5, ticker unchanged). Q2 recap: revenue $342.1M, adjusted EBITDA $193.2M, DCF coverage 1.65x, $0.525 distribution, full-year guidance confirmed (EBITDA $770-800M, DCF $480-510M). Units should track energy-sector beta and the rate tape — the US-Iran oil-talk pullback is a modest sector headwind if it sticks.
